name: Homo sapiens
what: Our own species, first known from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco about 315,000 years ago.
why: Every person alive today descends from African populations of this species.

sources.cite: Hublin, J.-J. et al., "New fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco and the pan-African origin of Homo sapiens", Nature 546, 289-292 (2017)
Richter, D. et al., "The age of the hominin fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco", Nature 546, 293-296 (2017)

name: Neanderthals
what: Strong, big-brained people of Ice Age Europe and western Asia; they made tools, used fire, wore ornaments and buried some of their dead.
why: They vanished about 40,000 years ago, soon after modern humans arrived; 1 to 2% of their DNA lives on in everyone outside Africa.

sources.cite: Higham, T. et al., "The timing and spatiotemporal patterning of Neanderthal disappearance", Nature 512, 306-309 (2014)
Prüfer, K. et al., "The complete genome sequence of a Neanderthal from the Altai Mountains", Nature 505, 43-49 (2014)

name: Denisovans
what: A sister group of the Neanderthals known mostly from DNA: a finger bone, teeth and two jaws from Siberia, Tibet and Laos.
why: People of Papua and Aboriginal Australians carry up to 5% Denisovan DNA, so Denisovans must also have lived far to the south-east.

sources.cite: Reich, D. et al., "Genetic history of an archaic hominin group from Denisova Cave in Siberia", Nature 468, 1053-1060 (2010)
Demeter, F. et al., "A Middle Pleistocene Denisovan molar from the Annamite Chain of northern Laos", Nature Communications 13, 2557 (2022)
Zhang, D. et al., "Denisovan DNA in Late Pleistocene sediments from Baishiya Karst Cave on the Tibetan Plateau", Science 370, 584-587 (2020)

name: Homo floresiensis
what: A metre-tall human with a chimp-sized brain on the island of Flores.
why: Isolated on an island for perhaps a million years, its ancestors shrank, like the island's dwarf elephants.

sources.cite: Sutikna, T. et al., "Revised stratigraphy and chronology for Homo floresiensis at Liang Bua in Indonesia", Nature 532, 366-369 (2016)

name: Homo luzonensis
what: A small human known from teeth and finger and toe bones in Callao Cave, Luzon.
why: Archaic humans crossed open sea to the Philippines long before modern humans.

sources.cite: Détroit, F. et al., "A new species of Homo from the Late Pleistocene of the Philippines", Nature 568, 181-186 (2019)

name: Homo naledi
what: A small-brained human with modern-looking hands and feet, from the Rising Star caves.
why: Shows that a "primitive" human survived late, alongside early Homo sapiens.

sources.cite: Dirks, P. et al., "The age of Homo naledi and associated sediments in the Rising Star Cave, South Africa", eLife 6, e24231 (2017)

name: Homo erectus (last)
what: The long-lived human species that first left Africa; its last known members lived on Java.
why: It survived on Java until about 110,000 years ago, when grassland gave way to rainforest.

sources.cite: Rizal, Y. et al., "Last appearance of Homo erectus at Ngandong, Java, 117,000-108,000 years ago", Nature 577, 381-385 (2020)
